title: Building Custom Modules
text: building custom module, need handle Shiny’s namespacing correctly. key insight : module’s custom inputs need namespaced NS(id). base module’s UI server functions receive bare id, namespaced version. Data processing requires access module’s inputs must happen inside moduleServer() block. base module’s server called outside moduleServer() block avoid double-namespacing issues.

title: Building Custom Modules
text: Let’s build custom module adds simple filtering checkbox scatterPlot module.

title: Building Custom Modules
text: Notice checkboxInput() uses ns("filter_setosa") namespace custom input, scatterPlotInputsUI() receives bare id. ensures base module creates inputs correct namespace.
code: library(vizModules)  minimalModuleUI <- function(id) {     ns <- NS(id)     tagList(         h4("Minimal Module Controls"),         # Custom input - uses the module's namespace         checkboxInput(ns("filter_setosa"), "Start with Setosa Only", value = FALSE),         hr(),         # Base module UI - pass the bare 'id', not ns(id)         scatterPlotInputsUI(id, iris)     ) }  minimalModuleOutput <- function(id) {     # Simply delegate to the base module's output UI     scatterPlotOutputUI(id) }

title: Building Custom Modules
text: pattern? moduleServer(id, ...) gives us access input$filter_setosa, namespaced wrapper’s id. calling scatterPlotServer(id, filtered_data) outside moduleServer() closure, base module attaches namespace UI, nested one. called scatterPlotServer() inside moduleServer() block, create nested namespaces like id-id-x_axis, wouldn’t match actual input IDs UI.
code: minimalModuleServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {     # Step 1: Process data inside a moduleServer block     # This gives us access to inputs namespaced to 'id' (our module's inputs)     filtered_data <- moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {         reactive({             req(data_reactive())             df <- data_reactive()              # Input specific to this custom module             if (isTRUE(input$filter_setosa)) {                 if ("Species" %in% names(df)) {                     df <- df[df$Species == "setosa", ]                 }             }             df         })     })      # Step 2: Call the base module server OUTSIDE the moduleServer block     # This is critical! If we called this inside the moduleServer above,     # scatterPlotServer would look for inputs at id-id-inputName instead of id-inputName     scatterPlotServer(id, filtered_data) }

title: Building Custom Modules
code: ui <- fluidPage(     titlePanel("Minimal Module Example"),     sidebarLayout(         sidebarPanel(             minimalModuleUI("demo")         ),         mainPanel(             minimalModuleOutput("demo")         )     ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {     # Pass a reactive data source to the module     minimalModuleServer("demo", reactive({         iris     })) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Flexible, Interactive Shiny Modules For Almost Any Plot
text: Including vizModules module Shiny application simple. package provides function returning example Shiny application module showcases functionality can used. example, can look createScatterPlotApp() function:
code: library(vizModules)  createScatterPlotApp <- function(data_list) {     # Validate input     stopifnot(is.list(data_list))     lapply(data_list, function(data) {         stopifnot(is.data.frame(data))     })      # UI definition     ui <- fluidPage(         useShinyjs(),         titlePanel("Modular scatterPlots"),         sidebarLayout(             sidebarPanel(                 # Add the module inputs UI for each data frame                 lapply(names(data_list), function(name) {                     tagList(                         scatterPlotInputsUI(name, data_list[[name]], title = h3(paste(name, "Settings"))),                         hr()                     )                 })             ),             mainPanel(                 # Add the module output UI for each data frame                 lapply(names(data_list), function(name) {                     tagList(scatterPlotOutputUI(name), br())                 })             )         )     )      # Server function     server <- function(input, output, session) {          # Add the module server for each data frame         lapply(names(data_list), function(name) {             scatterPlotServer(name, data = reactive(data_list[[name]]))         })     }      # Return the Shiny app     shinyApp(ui, server) }  data_list <- list("mtcars" = mtcars, "iris" = iris) createScatterPlotApp(data_list)

title: Flexible, Interactive Shiny Modules For Almost Any Plot
text: modules vizModules designed composed extended. can build higher-level modules add custom logic reusing full functionality base modules. ’s minimal example wrapping scatterPlot module add custom filtering logic: Key points building wrapper modules: Namespace handling: Use NS(id) wrapper’s custom inputs, pass bare id (namespaced) base module’s UI server functions. Data processing pattern: Process data inside moduleServer() block access wrapper’s namespaced inputs, call base module’s server function outside block avoid double-namespacing. Reactive data: Always pass reactive expressions wrapper underlying module servers. details, see vignette("custom-modules", package = "vizModules").
code: library(vizModules)  # Define the wrapper UI minimalWrapperUI <- function(id) {     ns <- NS(id)     tagList(         h4("Minimal Wrapper Controls"),         checkboxInput(ns("filter_setosa"), "Start with Setosa Only", value = FALSE),         hr(),         scatterPlotInputsUI(id, iris)     ) }  minimalWrapperOutput <- function(id) {     scatterPlotOutputUI(id) }  # Define the wrapper server minimalWrapperServer <- function(id, data_reactive) {     # 1. Process data in a moduleServer block to access inputs namespaced to 'id'     # We return the reactive expression produced by this block.     # Note: moduleServer returns the return value of the function it runs.     filtered_data <- moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {         reactive({             req(data_reactive())             df <- data_reactive()              # Custom wrapper logic: filter based on a checkbox             if (isTRUE(input$filter_setosa)) {                 if ("Species" %in% names(df)) {                     df <- df[df$Species == "setosa", ]                 }             }             df         })     })      # 2. Call the base module server with the processed data.     # We call this OUTSIDE the first moduleServer closure so that     # scatterPlotServer attaches to 'id' relative to the parent,     # avoiding nested namespace issues (e.g. id-id-input).     scatterPlotServer(id, filtered_data) }  # Create the app using the wrapper ui <- fluidPage(     titlePanel("Minimal Wrapper Example"),     sidebarLayout(         sidebarPanel(             minimalWrapperUI("demo")         ),         mainPanel(             minimalWrapperOutput("demo")         )     ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {     minimalWrapperServer("demo", reactive({ iris })) }  shinyApp(ui, server)
